preamble: Voicing of the velar ejective [kʼ] to [g]. Proto-Nakh ejectives (Nikolayev & Starostin 1994; Nichols 2003; Schrijver 2021) are kept in Bats (Tsova-Tush), the most conservative Nakh language. In Chechen and Ingush (Vainakh), single non-initial ejectives after a vowel or sonorant became voiced, while word-initial ejectives and *qʼ survive; geminate ejectives and ejectives after x instead lost glottalization but stayed voiceless. The velar series is the best attested, partly because many nouns end in the old diminutive suffix *-iḳ.
